{
  "winner": "B",
  "reasons": [
    "B has documented, sourced spending by the target payer. Cole County, MO paid $7,000 for an AI compliance tool in March 2026, and the Town of Templeton, MA was quoted $2,510 for AudioEye. A has competitor list prices but no evidence that anyone has actually paid, and one of its competitors (Insightloop) is pre-launch.",
    "B's pain is dated and externally forced: DOJ compliance deadlines of April 2027 for municipalities of 50,000+ and April 2028 for smaller ones, sourced to ADA.gov and the Federal Register. A's pain is a general feeling of decision paralysis with no forcing event.",
    "B's demand quotes come from named officials describing a compliance burden and a lack of IT staff. That maps directly onto buying a scanner. A's quotes describe a decision struggle but do not point to buying a research tool.",
    "B's price anchors ($149/month, $0.30/page, $2,510, $7,000) sit within range of a cheap free-audit lead funnel costing $10–$209/month in tooling. A's own brief concedes that a ~$104 cost per lead clashes with a ~$60 one-off price, and its organic channel is unquantified.",
    "Both markets are crowded with incumbents. A's competitors sell nearly the same product to the same buyer, and the category admits its outputs need human verification. B's incumbents leave room for a commodity scan plus prioritized-fix-list layer aimed at under-resourced small municipalities.",
    "B's main risks are real and weigh against the 90-day goal: slow municipal procurement, liability for compliance claims, and possible further deadline slippage. On balance, sourced evidence of actual government spending under deadline pressure outweighs A's thinner and partly self-undermining demand signal."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "A's demand evidence is two social posts, and the LinkedIn one ('Once you've got 2 real options, the spreadsheet can't choose between them. Only you can.') argues against outsourcing the decision to a tool. Neither post shows willingness to pay.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate confidence. B's evidence is clearly stronger, but its biggest threat to a paying customer within 90 days is the procurement burden the brief itself flags (RFPs, insurance certificates, vendor vetting), and no procurement timeline is quantified. A could close a card-paying individual faster, but its brief gives no evidence that such buyers exist at a price that covers acquisition cost."
}
